A micro-pilot resource auto-profiler that empirically measures peak RAM & runtime and computes optimal SLURM array chunking, memory, and walltime. 2. title: Getting Started with slurmpilot
text: Running large Monte Carlo power studies, hierarchical models, bootstraps SLURM cluster usually forces researchers manual batch scripting blind guesses --mem, --time, array chunking. slurmpilot replaces guesswork empirical, reproducible four-stage pipeline: Micro-pilot profiling (pilot_run()): Executes small sample slice isolated child R processes polling real OS resident memory (RSS) via ps. Resource auto-sizing (estimate_resources()): Computes optimal array chunk sizes, --mem, --time, --cpus-per-task flags tail-safe margins. Pluggable execution (MockSlurmBackend / SlurmSshBackend): Develop test complete lifecycle locally parallel background R processes laptop, switch SSH/SLURM zero workflow rewrites. Atomic checkpoints & surgical retries (slurm_retry(), slurm_collect()): Every chunk writes atomic .rds checkpoint protected SHA-256 sidecar failed OOM chunks retry cleanly without recomputing completed work.

title: From Micro-Pilot Profiling to Load-Balanced SLURM Arrays
text: Real statistical computing jobs rarely uniform, symmetric runtimes. Parameter grids often sweep sample sizes small large, iterative estimators (MCMC, mixed models, optimization) produce strongly right-skewed runtime tails. vignette covers three pillars accurate HPC sizing slurmpilot: Empirical OS-level RSS runtime profiling pilot_run(). Tail-safe walltime scaling skewed/heavy-tailed workloads estimate_resources(). Heterogeneous chunk load balancing (contiguous, round_robin, Longest Processing Time first lpt) plus pre-submit closure auditing inspect_job_globals().

title: From Micro-Pilot Profiling to Load-Balanced SLURM Arrays
text: pilot_run() runs sample replications isolated background child processes (isolate = TRUE) polling OS process-tree RSS via ps. Using sample_method = "stratified" samples evenly across ordered parameter grid inexpensive expensive cells profiled:
code: library(slurmpilot)  grid <- lapply(seq_len(12L), function(i) {   list(task_id = i, n = 100L + 50L * i, reps = 30L) })  sim_worker <- function(cfg) {   vals <- replicate(cfg$reps, mean(stats::rnorm(cfg$n)))   data.frame(task_id = cfg$task_id, n = cfg$n, est_se = stats::sd(vals)) }  pilot <- pilot_run(   fun = sim_worker,   args_list = grid,   n_pilot = 3L,   sample_method = "stratified",   seed = 101L )  print(pilot) #>  #> ── slurmpilot Micro-Pilot Profile #> • Trials: 3/3 succeeded (isolated=TRUE, cpus=1) #> • Task exec time: median 0.002s, p90 0.002s, max 0.002s #> • Worker startup: median 0.289s #> • Memory (RSS): baseline 76.3 MB, peak max 76.6 MB, net max 0.4 MB summary(pilot) #> # A tibble: 13 × 2 #>    metric                    value #>    <chr>                     <dbl> #>  1 n_trials                3       #>  2 n_ok                    3       #>  3 n_failed                0       #>  4 startup_median_sec      0.289   #>  5 exec_mean_sec           0.00200 #>  6 exec_sd_sec             0       #>  7 exec_q50_sec            0.00200 #>  8 exec_q90_sec            0.00200 #>  9 exec_q95_sec            0.00200 #> 10 exec_max_sec            0.00200 #> 11 baseline_rss_median_mb 76.3     #> 12 peak_rss_max_mb        76.6     #> 13 net_rss_max_mb          0.352 plot(pilot, engine = "base")

text: pilot runtimes exhibit right skew (instance, MCMC chain optimizer 4 trials take ~1 second 1 trial takes 40 seconds), naive normal Central Limit Theorem (CLT) bound underestimates upper-tail chunk walltime. estimate_resources() evaluates robust three-model envelope: Tpred(k)=t̂0+max⁡(QCLT(k),Q0.99LogNormal(k),QNonparametric(k))T_{\text{pred}}(k) = \hat{t}_0 + \max\!\left(Q^{\text{CLT}}(k),\; Q^{\text{LogNormal}}_{0.99}(k),\; Q^{\text{Nonparametric}}(k)\right) combining normal CLT, Fenton-Wilkinson log-normal sum approximation, nonparametric order-statistic bound. demonstrate scaling model detects heavy tails protects --time automatically:
code: skew_trials <- tibble::tibble(   trial_id = 1:5,   task_index = 1:5,   status = rep("OK", 5),   wall_sec = c(3.0, 3.2, 3.1, 3.3, 42.0),   startup_sec = rep(2.0, 5),   exec_sec = c(1.0, 1.2, 1.1, 1.3, 40.0),   baseline_rss_mb = rep(110, 5),   peak_rss_mb = c(240, 260, 255, 270, 390),   net_rss_mb = c(130, 150, 145, 160, 280),   cpu_user_sec = c(1.0, 1.2, 1.1, 1.3, 39.5),   cpu_sys_sec = rep(0.1, 5),   n_samples = rep(12L, 5),   result_size_bytes = rep(1024, 5),   error = rep(NA_character_, 5) )  skew_pilot <- structure(   list(     trials = skew_trials,     summary = list(       n_trials = 5L, n_ok = 5L, n_failed = 0L, n_timeout = 0L, n_oom_suspect = 0L,       failure_rate = 0, exec_mean_sec = mean(skew_trials$exec_sec),       exec_sd_sec = stats::sd(skew_trials$exec_sec),       exec_q50_sec = stats::median(skew_trials$exec_sec),       exec_q90_sec = stats::quantile(skew_trials$exec_sec, 0.90, names = FALSE),       startup_median_sec = 2.0, baseline_rss_median_mb = 110,       peak_rss_max_mb = 390, net_rss_max_mb = 280     ),     meta = list(n_pilot = 5L, n_total_hint = 100L, cpus_per_task = 1L, isolate = TRUE)   ),   class = "slurmpilot_pilot" )  res_skew <- estimate_resources(   skew_pilot,   n_tasks = 100L,   max_chunk_size = 5L,   partition = "general" ) print(res_skew) #>  #> ── slurmpilot SLURM Resource Plan #> • Workload: 100 tasks -> 20 array chunks (5 tasks/chunk) #> • SLURM flags: --array=1-20 --cpus-per-task=1 --mem=768M --time=00:30:00 #>   --partition=general #> ℹ Predicted chunk walltime: 1002.0s (expected 46.6s, startup overhead 4.3%) #> ℹ Predicted peak RSS: 435.3 MB -> requested 768M #> ℹ Estimated total compute: 0.26 CPU-hours res_skew$estimates[c("dominant_model", "is_heavy_tailed", "pred_clt_sec", "pred_lognormal_sec", "pred_nonparametric_sec")] #> $dominant_model #> [1] "lognormal" #>  #> $is_heavy_tailed #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $pred_clt_sec #> [1] 182.5778 #>  #> $pred_lognormal_sec #> [1] 1002 #>  #> $pred_nonparametric_sec #> [1] 163.3

what: 3. Heterogeneous Load Balancing: Contiguous vs Round-Robin vs LPT
title: From Micro-Pilot Profiling to Load-Balanced SLURM Arrays
text: tasks vary widely cost (example, sample sizes MCMC chain lengths spanning order magnitude), contiguous slicing packs expensive tasks final chunk, creating single straggler stalls array job. Compare plan_chunks() across "contiguous", "round_robin", "lpt" (Longest Processing Time first greedy makespan minimization): Execute LPT-balanced array job locally verify slurm_collect() automatically restores exact 1..N task ordering regardless chunk assignment:
code: task_costs <- c(10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30, 50, 60, 80, 95, 110, 130)  p_contig <- plan_chunks(length(task_costs), chunk_size = 3L, strategy = "contiguous", task_weights = task_costs) p_rr     <- plan_chunks(length(task_costs), chunk_size = 3L, strategy = "round_robin", task_weights = task_costs) p_lpt    <- plan_chunks(length(task_costs), chunk_size = 3L, strategy = "lpt", task_weights = task_costs)  comparison <- data.frame(   strategy = c("contiguous", "round_robin", "lpt"),   max_chunk_cost = c(     max(p_contig$estimated_weight),     max(p_rr$estimated_weight),     max(p_lpt$estimated_weight)   ),   imbalance_ratio = round(c(     max(p_contig$estimated_weight) / mean(p_contig$estimated_weight),     max(p_rr$estimated_weight) / mean(p_rr$estimated_weight),     max(p_lpt$estimated_weight) / mean(p_lpt$estimated_weight)   ), 3) ) print(comparison) #>      strategy max_chunk_cost imbalance_ratio #> 1  contiguous            335           2.104 #> 2 round_robin            210           1.319 #> 3         lpt            165           1.036 tmp_root <- tempfile("sp_lpt_") be <- mock_slurm_backend(root_dir = tmp_root, max_workers = 2L)  res_lpt <- resource_spec(   n_tasks = length(grid),   chunk_size = 3L,   mem_mb = 512L,   time_minutes = 5,   strategy = "lpt",   task_weights = task_costs )  job <- slurm_submit(be, sim_worker, grid, resources = res_lpt, name = "lpt_sim", seed = 77L) st <- slurm_wait(job, timeout = 30, poll_interval = 0.05) out <- slurm_collect(job, simplify = TRUE)  stopifnot(identical(out$task_id, seq_len(length(grid)))) head(out) #> # A tibble: 6 × 3 #>   task_id     n est_se #>     <int> <int>  <dbl> #> 1       1   150 0.0913 #> 2       2   200 0.0676 #> 3       3   250 0.0613 #> 4       4   300 0.0591 #> 5       5   350 0.0491 #> 6       6   400 0.0470  unlink(tmp_root, recursive = TRUE)

title: Multi-Stage HPC Pipelines, Efficiency Auditing & Container Handoff
text: Production computational statistics workflows rarely stop single isolated array job. Researchers commonly run multi-stage dependent pipelines (example, simulate across parallel array chunks, branch independent summary diagnostic stages, fan-final synthesis table), audit cluster efficiency post-mortem tighten future SLURM requests, attach reproducible Apptainer containers produced external tools rcapsule. vignette demonstrates three workflows introduced slurmpilot 0.4.0.

title: Multi-Stage HPC Pipelines, Efficiency Auditing & Container Handoff
text: slurm_stage() slurm_pipeline() assemble dependent array stages directed acyclic graph (DAG), automatically validating unique names, upstream references, acyclicity via Kahn’s topological sort. construct four-stage diamond DAG: - simulate (root): runs 8 parallel Monte Carlo estimation tasks. - power_summary (branch ): dynamically consumes simulate outputs via args_from_upstream compute chunk-level rejection indicators. - bias_summary (branch B): computes bias summaries across simulated estimates using .upstream$simulate. - synthesize (fan-sink): waits power_summary bias_summary (afterok) combines final summary record. Execute entire diamond DAG locally MockSlurmBackend (capped 2 workers) inspect live stage status final collected results:
code: library(slurmpilot)  s_sim <- slurm_stage(   name = "simulate",   fun = function(cfg) {     x <- stats::rnorm(cfg$n, mean = cfg$delta, sd = 1)     tt <- stats::t.test(x, mu = 0)     data.frame(       task_id = cfg$task_id,       est = mean(x),       reject = tt$p.value < 0.05     )   },   args_list = lapply(seq_len(8L), function(i) list(task_id = i, n = 40L, delta = 0.4)),   resources = resource_spec(n_tasks = 8L, chunk_size = 4L, mem_mb = 512L, time_minutes = 5),   seed = 2026L )  s_power <- slurm_stage(   name = "power_summary",   fun = function(row_df) mean(row_df$reject),   args_from_upstream = function(up) split(up$simulate, up$simulate$task_id <= 4L),   depends_on = "simulate" )  s_bias <- slurm_stage(   name = "bias_summary",   fun = function(target_delta) mean(.upstream$simulate$est) - target_delta,   args_list = list(0.4),   depends_on = "simulate" )  s_final <- slurm_stage(   name = "synthesize",   fun = function(up) {     data.frame(       empirical_power = mean(up$power_summary),       mean_bias = mean(up$bias_summary)     )   },   depends_on = c("power_summary", "bias_summary") )  pipe <- slurm_pipeline(s_sim, s_power, s_bias, s_final, name = "mc_diamond") print(pipe) #>  #> ── slurmpilot Pipeline DAG: mc_diamond #> • Stages: 4 | Edges: 4 | Roots: simulate | Sinks: synthesize #> • Topological order: simulate -> power_summary -> bias_summary -> synthesize tmp_dag <- tempfile("sp_dag_") be_local <- mock_slurm_backend(root_dir = tmp_dag, max_workers = 2L)  run <- slurm_pipeline_run(pipe, be_local, wait = TRUE, poll_interval = 0.05) print(slurm_pipeline_status(run)) #>  #> ── slurmpilot Pipeline Status: mc_diamond [COMPLETED] #> • Stages completed: 4/4 (running=0, pending=0, failed=0, skipped=0) slurm_pipeline_status(run)$stages[, c("stage", "level", "state", "n_chunks")] #> # A tibble: 4 × 4 #>   stage         level state     n_chunks #>   <chr>         <int> <chr>        <int> #> 1 simulate          1 COMPLETED        2 #> 2 power_summary     2 COMPLETED        1 #> 3 bias_summary      2 COMPLETED        1 #> 4 synthesize        3 COMPLETED        1  slurm_pipeline_collect(run, simplify = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   empirical_power mean_bias #>             <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1            0.75    0.0204

title: Troubleshooting, Adaptive Retries & Reproducible Parallel RNG
text: Large HPC array jobs fail predictable ways: handful outlier tasks hit OUT_OF_MEMORY TIMEOUT, shared network filesystems suffer partial writes, naive parallel seeding silently correlates Monte Carlo replications across compute nodes. vignette demonstrates slurmpilot handles three failure modes deterministically.

what: 1. Adaptive Escalation for OOM and Timeout Failures
title: Troubleshooting, Adaptive Retries & Reproducible Parallel RNG
text: slurm_retry(job, adaptive = TRUE) (default) inspects failed array chunks: Chunks OUT_OF_MEMORY automatically trigger --mem escalation (default 1.5x, bounded max_mem_mb). Chunks TIMEOUT automatically trigger --time escalation (default 1.5x, bounded max_time_minutes). Already-completed chunks never re-executed; atomic checkpoints remain untouched disk. Every escalation event logged per-chunk retry provenance via slurm_retry_history(job). Let us simulate 4-chunk job chunk 2 suffers OUT_OF_MEMORY kill chunk 4 suffers TIMEOUT kill attempt 1: Calling slurm_retry(job) zero manual flags detects failure causes, escalates --mem (512 MB -> 768 MB) --time (10 min -> 15 min), resubmits chunks 2 4:
code: library(slurmpilot)  tmp_root <- tempfile("sp_troubleshoot_") be <- mock_slurm_backend(root_dir = tmp_root, max_workers = 2L)  res <- resource_spec(n_tasks = 8L, chunk_size = 2L, mem_mb = 512L, time_minutes = 10) job <- slurm_submit(   backend = be,   fun = function(x) x^3,   args_list = as.list(seq_len(8L)),   resources = res,   name = "adaptive_demo",   seed = 2026L,   fault_injection = list(oom_chunks = 2L, timeout_chunks = 4L, fail_once = TRUE) )  st1 <- slurm_wait(job, timeout = 30, poll_interval = 0.05) st1$chunks[, c("chunk_id", "state", "attempt", "checkpoint_exists")] #> # A tibble: 4 × 4 #>   chunk_id state         attempt checkpoint_exists #>      <int> <chr>           <int> <lgl>             #> 1        1 COMPLETED           1 TRUE              #> 2        2 OUT_OF_MEMORY       1 FALSE             #> 3        3 COMPLETED           1 TRUE              #> 4        4 TIMEOUT             1 FALSE job <- slurm_retry(job) st2 <- slurm_wait(job, timeout = 30, poll_interval = 0.05) print(st2) #>  #> ── slurmpilot Job Status: adaptive_demo [COMPLETED] #> • Progress: 4/4 chunks (100%) | running=0, pending=0, failed=0, oom=0, #>   timeout=0, cancelled=0 #> • Peak RSS max: 73.4 MB | Cumulative walltime: 0.17s  # Inspect recorded retry provenance slurm_retry_history(job) #> # A tibble: 2 × 9 #>   retry_round timestamp             chunk_id trigger_state old_mem_mb new_mem_mb #>         <int> <chr>                    <int> <chr>              <int>      <int> #> 1           1 2026-11-24T21:06:59.…        2 OUT_OF_MEMORY        512        768 #> 2           1 2026-11-24T21:06:59.…        4 TIMEOUT              512        768 #> # ℹ 3 more variables: old_time_sec <int>, new_time_sec <int>, adaptive <lgl>  # Verify completed results in exact 1..8 order slurm_collect(job, simplify = TRUE) #> [1]   1   8  27  64 125 216 343 512

what: 2. Detecting and Healing Corrupted Checkpoints via SHA-256
title: Troubleshooting, Adaptive Retries & Reproducible Parallel RNG
text: Every completed chunk writes results/chunk_XXXX.rds atomically (temp file + file.rename()) paired cryptographic SHA-256 sidecar (results/chunk_XXXX.rds.sha256). verify_checkpoint() slurm_collect() validate every digest deserialization silent Lustre/NFS truncation bit rot can never poison downstream inference:
code: cp2 <- file.path(job$local_dir, "results", "chunk_0002.rds") verify_checkpoint(cp2, require_sidecar = TRUE)$ok #> [1] TRUE  # Simulate a single corrupted byte on disk raw_bytes <- readBin(cp2, what = "raw", n = file.info(cp2)$size) raw_bytes[[length(raw_bytes)]] <- xor(raw_bytes[[length(raw_bytes)]], as.raw(0xFF)) writeBin(raw_bytes, cp2)  # Integrity verifier catches the mismatch immediately chk <- verify_checkpoint(cp2) chk$ok #> [1] FALSE chk$reason #> [1] "SHA-256 sidecar mismatch (expected 6fa0d2046e32d048c15fefbb02f016ef94d78444513c64212cb1ee3ad0e7b411, got bfaf6d52f076580f35e12f1dab72e3f378af7ef91ae7e886ca4ad4b4d72ec505)."  # Surgical retry of chunk 2 heals the corrupted checkpoint cleanly job <- slurm_retry(job, chunks = 2L, adaptive = FALSE) st3 <- slurm_wait(job, timeout = 30, poll_interval = 0.05) verify_checkpoint(cp2, require_sidecar = TRUE)$ok #> [1] TRUE slurm_collect(job, simplify = TRUE) #> [1]   1   8  27  64 125 216 343 512

title: Troubleshooting, Adaptive Retries & Reproducible Parallel RNG
text: Seeding parallel array jobs naive consecutive integers (set.seed(seed + )) guarantee non-overlapping random-number streams. slurmpilot’s standalone worker.R initializes base R’s L'Ecuyer-CMRG generator uses parallel::nextRNGStream() (21272^{127} draws chunks) combined parallel::nextRNGSubStream() (2762^{76} draws tasks within chunk). can inspect reproduce (seed, chunk_id, task_pos) stream directly via slurmpilot_rng_stream() without mutating global .Random.seed:
code: s_c1_t1 <- slurmpilot_rng_stream(2026L, chunk_id = 1L, task_pos = 1L) s_c2_t1 <- slurmpilot_rng_stream(2026L, chunk_id = 2L, task_pos = 1L) !identical(s_c1_t1, s_c2_t1) #> [1] TRUE  rng_job <- slurm_submit(   backend = be,   fun = function(i) list(kind = RNGkind()[[1L]], draws = stats::rnorm(200)),   args_list = as.list(seq_len(6L)),   resources = resource_spec(n_tasks = 6L, chunk_size = 2L),   name = "rng_verify",   seed = 2026L ) slurm_wait(rng_job, timeout = 30, poll_interval = 0.05) #>  #> ── slurmpilot Job Status: rng_verify [COMPLETED] #> • Progress: 3/3 chunks (100%) | running=0, pending=0, failed=0, oom=0, #>   timeout=0, cancelled=0 #> • Peak RSS max: 74.0 MB | Cumulative walltime: 0.10s rng_out <- slurm_collect(rng_job)  # All workers used L'Ecuyer-CMRG and produced empirically uncorrelated streams all(vapply(rng_out, function(x) x$kind == "L'Ecuyer-CMRG", logical(1L))) #> [1] TRUE cor_mat <- stats::cor(do.call(cbind, lapply(rng_out, `[[`, "draws"))) diag(cor_mat) <- 0 round(max(abs(cor_mat)), 3) #> [1] 0.144  unlink(tmp_root, recursive = TRUE)
